ads.title: Backyard Legends
ads.description: Adidas's headline World Cup spot for 2026, set in the streets and side-lots where the brand's roster — Messi, Bad Bunny, Yamal, Bellingham, Trinity Rodman — first started playing. A 90s-flavored film built on the bet that legends are forged in backyard games, not stadium tunnels. The 'You Got This' platform delivered with the largest celebrity density of the wave so far.

ads.title: All the Feels
ads.description: Coca-Cola's tournament platform-launch and the opener of a three-film 'All the Feels' arc. Leans on pre-match anticipation as the emotional center. Soft-launches the new Coke World Cup anthem — a J Balvin / Amber Mark / Steve Vai / Travis Barker rework of an '80s rock track — without leaning on it.

ads.title: Leo Messi: For You, the Fans
ads.description: Hyundai's Messi-led brand film, folded into a broader children's-dreams platform that ties their team-bus design program to fans worldwide. Leo carries the spot; the campaign sits in service. Reads more institutional than memorable, which appears to be the brief.

ads.title: Get Access to FIFA World Cup 2026
ads.description: Visa's co-branded play with Marriott Bonvoy: travel, payments, and host-city access bundled as a single tournament proposition. Restrained, premium tone — built for an exec audience and the access-economy fan.

ads.title: Let It Pour
ads.description: Grey Global's Haaland and Klopp showcase, directed by MJZ's Steve Ayson and scored to Joe Cocker. Klopp anchors from a bar; cuts pull through fans worldwide; Haaland scores; a Godzilla cameo lands the punchline. Less interested in goosebumps than in making fans grin. Highest replay value in the early wave.

ads.title: The Most Epic Watch Party
ads.description: Lay's reactivates 'No Lay's, No Game' for 2026 with a fictional WhatsApp watch party — Messi, Beckham, Henry, Putellas, Steve Carell — all stuck on the same group chat. Carell's presence in particular pulls the spot away from reverence and into something more shareable.

ads.title: Our Host
ads.description: Hisense's tournament platform launch — culture-led, experience-driven, partnered with Crews on a long-term content arc across film, social and retail. A pivot away from the spec-sheet TV ads of past Cups.

ads.title: Power Your Fate
ads.description: Powerade's preparation-meets-performance frame: the brand positions itself as the fuel between off-season and decisive moments. Heavy on the readiness-rituals territory, distributed across global TV, digital and creator content.

ads.title: Superior Player of the Match Trophy
ads.description: Michelob Ultra leans into its Anheuser-Busch sibling's tournament rights with a cheeky 'Superior Player' trophy hand-off bit. Performance-marketing spend behind it; brand-storytelling restraint up front.

ads.title: The Home of Football Banter & Rivalry
ads.description: Pepsi continues the tournament tradition with a banter-and-rivalry frame, stacking Messi, Ronaldo, Mbappé and Vinícius Jr. into the kind of all-stars vignette that travels well in social cuts. Doubles down on creativity-and-play over reverence.

ads.title: Celebration ft. David Beckham
ads.description: Stella's premium-toned Beckham vehicle. Frames the brand around hospitality and togetherness during matches — 'home advantage' as the emotional center, played in a slower, quieter register than the Bud line in the same portfolio.

ads.title: Everyone Wants a Piece
ads.description: Lego's tournament play stacks Messi, Ronaldo, Mbappé and Vinícius Jr. into a brick-built world where football fandom and creative play are the same posture. Among the highest social-share rates in the early wave — kid-coded but parent-aimed.
